claims.text: Directly coating a Cu substrate with a conventional high-entropy alloy can result in poor adhesion.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between Cu and a conventional HEA contributes to poor coating adhesion.
Crystal-structure mismatch between Cu and a conventional HEA contributes to poor coating adhesion.
A Cu-enriched HEA interlayer can be deposited by a controlled process such as magnetron sputtering.
The interlayer composition can be graded from pure Cu at the substrate interface to a conventional HEA at the top surface.
The graded interlayer will produce a gradual interdiffusion zone.
The graded interfacial composition will reduce lattice-structure disparities across the interface.
The graded interfacial composition will reduce disparities in thermal-expansion coefficients across the interface.
Incorporating Cu into the interlayer improves chemical compatibility with the Cu substrate.
Minimizing abrupt interfacial property changes lowers residual stress.
The graded interface promotes a stronger metallurgical bond.
A stronger metallurgical bond enhances coating adhesion.
The graded Cu-enriched interlayer will improve wear resistance.
The graded Cu-enriched interlayer will provide higher adhesion strength than direct deposition of a conventional HEA on Cu.
The graded Cu-enriched interlayer will lower wear rates under cyclic thermal and frictional stress relative to a directly deposited HEA coating.
Directly deposited conventional HEA coatings on Cu have historically exhibited weak adhesion.
Directly deposited conventional HEA coatings on Cu have reduced durability under thermal and mechanical cycling.
Insufficient compositional grading or uncontrolled interfacial reactions may limit adhesion improvement.
